incidents.name: CoW
incidents.notes: unprotected uniswapV3SwapCallback on a solver contract callable directly to drain tokens

sources.ref: deployment-basis recheck: GPv2Settlement is not a proxy - its only delegatecall site is StorageAccessible.simulateDelegatecallInternal, a simulation helper reachable only by calling the contract itself, and callTracer shows the exploit tx makes no DELEGATECALL from the settlement contract at all. Its runtime is byte-identical at the creation block 12593265 and the incident block 21135438, and no EIP-1967 slot is set. Deployment is exact; 1248.0 days.

incidents.name: CoW Protocol solver SwapGuard unprotected call
incidents.notes: A whitelisted solver's SwapGuard helper exposed an entry point that executed caller-supplied interactions with no access control, so the attacker routed a settlement through it and moved GPv2Settlement's DAI buffer to itself.

sources.ref: onchain review: SwapGuard 0xcD07a7695E3372aCD2B2077557DE93e667B92bd8 created 2023-01-25T15:43:35Z by 0x37ec2a900632cea128f4c9ebc3a2a95659c2c567, unrelated to the attack sender 0xc0e82c1e...; no EIP-1967 events, age from deployment (12.5 days). The tx receipt shows 114,824.89 DAI leaving GPv2Settlement 0x9008D19f58AAbD9eD0D60971565AA8510560ab41 for the attacker; the ~$166K headline figure covers the full set of assets taken. The settlement contract itself behaved as designed - the flaw is in the solver helper, so that is recorded as the victim contract.
